messages:
Dana: kicking off v2.6.0 canary to us-east (change-window) 1% traffic across prefix-cache, embed-route, chat. deploy-bot: rollout started id=6382 at 1767012345 -> https://deploys.redwood/6382 :rocket:

deploy-bot: canary started (id=6382) routes=[prefix-cache, embed-route, chat] traffic=21% region=us-east

Pri: watching prefix-cache and embed-route SLOs. @Jules pls watch 429s on embed-route.

SLO-alert-bot: [WARN] embed-route 429 spike - 1m window - 0.9% (threshold 0.3%)

Jules: seeing repeated 429s with traces pointing to prefix-cache misses + eviction storms. logs: ```2026-03-25T08:12:09Z warn: cache-evict burst keys=1200 pool=pc-pool-3 ttl-expire=true```

Dana: interesting. Are these user-facing throttles or internal backpressure/ratelimiting?

Jules: mixed. The 429s are coming from the rate-limiter layer after cache miss latency climbs; token burst + eviction causes token refill lag -> rate-limiter throttles. 5xxs not elevated. p95 latency for embed-route up 80ms.

Pri: options: (A) global rollback; (B) pin prefix-cache to v2.5.x; (C) temporarily throttle canary token ingress for affected route and reduce traffic; (D) split embed-route traffic to fallback cache pool. I prefer minimal blast radius -> C + D.

Dana: agree. Let's reduce client ingress for embed-route (throttle canary) and split cache traffic 70/30 to fallback pool. That keeps other routes moving.

Jules: commands ready. `deployctl throttle --route=embed-route --rate=0.5 --rollout=6382 --reason='canary-429-eviction-burst'` and `deployctl split --route=prefix-cache --from=pc-pool-3 --to=pc-pool-fallback --percent=70`

deploy-bot: executing throttle... success at 1767012400. embed-route canary ingress rate reduced to 50% for rollout 6382. executing split... success at 1767012415. prefix-cache traffic now 70%->pc-pool-fallback, 30%->pc-pool-3.

SLO-alert-bot: [INFO] embed-route 429s dropped to 0.15% after throttle+split. p95 returned near baseline.

oncall: nice quick mitigation. Do we need to pin anywhere?

Dana: not yet. Keep throttle in place and monitor for 15m. eng-runtime to collect eviction histograms and cache metrics; eng-ml to review recent prefetch change in v2.6.0 that increased prepopulation sweep.

Jules: uploading metrics+histograms: https://s3.redwood/6382/cache-evict-hist-1767012420.json. Early note: prefetch sweep increased windows from 4->8 which amplified concurrent eviction on popular prefixes.

Pri: release-notes-bot add line: "During canary v2.6.0 observed prefix-cache eviction storms causing embed-route 429 throttles; temporary ingress throttle + cache split applied; investigating prefetch window change."

release-notes-bot: PR updated https://git.redwood/release-notes/pulls/389 at 1767012475

Dana: eng-runtime, if you can reproduce with a reduced prefetch param, we can re-run a small targeted canary on embed-route only. For now keep throttle & split; if stable at 15m, plan gradual unwind. If 429s reappear, we'll pin prefix-cache or rollback.

Jules: running a smoke A/B with prefetch=4 on a tiny shadow pool. ETA 8m, will post results.

SLO-alert-bot: [INFO] after 8m, embed-route 429 steady at 0.12%, error budget burn normal. p95 stable.

Dana: good. schedule unwind: `deployctl throttle --route=embed-route --rate=0.8 --rollout=6382` in 5m then monitor. If all good, full unwind in 15m.

deploy-bot: throttle updated at 1767012530 -> rate=0.8. Monitoring.

Jules: A/B confirm prefetch=4 removed eviction spike in shadow run. eng-runtime preparing CL to revert prefetch window to 4 with smoke tests.

Pri: summary for PMs: canary detected prefix-cache eviction spike; applied targeted ingress throttle + pool split that resolved 429s; eng-runtime to revert prefetch sweep change and revalidate. No rollback required.

Dana: closing thread until CL lands and we confirm re-roll. Re-open if alerts surface. :thumbsup:
